text:
sophia: Hey team, customer ACME reports p99 latency jumped from 240ms -> 1.2s around 10:20 UTC, started ~1h ago. No error spikes, just tail latency. Service: redwood-prod-us-west, model: vicuna-13b-8k-q4, tenant: acme-main.
emma: Noted. Any correlating deploys or autoscale events? infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary rollout redwood-runtime v2.14 -> v2.15 at 10:12 UTC (canary 10%).
mike: Can confirm, saw increased GPU memory pressure on a subset of hosts in us-west-2 around 10:15. p95/99 rise aligns. Attaching heatmap snippet.
emma: Can you paste the top oom logs / KV cache stats? even a short snippet helps.
mike: Logs: "gpu_mem_used=22.1G gpu_mem_total=24.0G free=1.9G slab_frag=0.42 kv_entries=1.2M kv_bytes=11.3G"
emma: kv_entries looks high for that cluster. Any tenant-specific KV growth for ACME?
raj: Oncall-runtime chiming in — we rolled a change to alloc behavior in v2.15: slab eviction threshold lowered to 0.6 -> 0.55 (more aggressive alloc packing) plus a small KV retention tweak. Hypothesis: new allocator+KV retention interaction causing fragmentation and async OOM backpressure.
sophia: ACME is heavy on short-chats with many system prompts and dynamic assistant sketches -> lots of KV churn.
emma: Short mitigation options: 1) increase canary rollback to 0% (quick), 2) force KV eviction for ACME route, 3) temporarily pin ACME to older runtime (v2.14). Which is fastest?
mike: Rollback canary to 0% now. Rolling back canary and pin ACME to v2.14 as safe fallback while we triage.
raj: I'll run a hotfix branch to revert the allocator tweak and instrument more KV eviction metrics. Need ~15min to compile and validate.
emma: Going to message ACME with ETA: "we've detected GPU memory pressure causing tail latency, rolling back a recent runtime change and pinning your traffic to previous runtime — expected mitigation in ~20m" :thumbsup:
sophia: Thanks. Also capturing repro steps: high concurrency synthetic traffic with 3-4 short messages and many unique system prompts triggers KV entries growth. Repro script attached (short):
```
for i in range(1000):
  client.chat.create(model='vicuna-13b-8k-q4', prompt=f"system: {uuid4()}; user: hi")
  sleep(0.01)
```

mike: After rollback start at 10:30, observed GPU free rise to ~4.5G and p99 fell from 1.2s -> 260ms by 10:40. Initial mitigation looks effective.
emma: Good. Raj, once you have the hotfix build, can you run a controlled canary with KV eviction logging and a synthetic workload? We need to validate no regression in throughput/latency and confirm slab fragmentation reduced.
raj: Yes. Hotfix built, deploying to canary group now with extra flags: `--kv-evict-threshold=0.7 --alloc-compact=true` and added eviction metrics. Starting canary run.
infra-bot: [metric-alert] kv_evictions increased x12 on canary nodes; slab_frag dropped 0.42 -> 0.18; gpu_free increased by ~1.1G.
mike: Can confirm p99 on canary under synthetic load ~270ms stable. Looks good. Let's schedule gradual rollout to remaining canaries and then to prod after 1h observation.
emma: For immediate customer-facing notes: update ACME ticket saying rollback completed and we're rolling hotfix. Set follow-up for root cause analysis with eng-runtime tomorrow.
sophia: I'll mark ticket as "mitigated" and ask ACME for any residual latency observations over the next 24h.
raj: Postmortem action items: 1) Add KV per-tenant growth alert when kv_entries rate > X/s, 2) improve allocator canary invariants, 3) add a compact-on-evict background job, 4) update rollout checklist to monitor slab_frag and kv_evictions.
emma: Also add a temporary tenant-level knob to limit per-request KV growth (truncate system messages > N) — product will review.
mike: I'll create infra metric dashboards for slab_frag, kv_entries, kv_evictions, and gpu_free per-route.
emma: Thanks all — leaving thread open for 24h follow-ups. If ACME reports reoccurrence, escalate to @raj and @mike immediately.
sophia: ACME replied: "latency back to normal, thanks for the quick fix". Closing loop. :tada:
